title: Make.com in 2026: agents that act, not just automations that wait
content:
For years, Make (formerly Integromat) was the visual canvas you used to wire apps together: a trigger fires, modules run, data moves. Powerful, but reactive. It waited for something to happen.

In 2026 that is shifting. Make's big bet is AI Agents built right into the Scenario Builder, and the framing is sharp: agents become workflow engines that detect work, decide what to do, and complete multi-step tasks without waiting for a human to press go.

What is actually new:

1. Agents inside the canvas. The next-gen agents live in the same visual builder you already know, with a reasoning panel so you can see why an agent made a decision, not just what it did. That visibility is the whole point: automation you can audit.

2. Multimodal inputs. Agents can take documents, images, and audio as context, so they are not limited to clean text fields. That opens up a lot of real-world use cases.

3. Reusable agent libraries. Build an agent once, then reuse and share it across scenarios, so a team assembles a library of agents instead of rebuilding the same logic everywhere.

4. Model choice. Agents are not locked to one LLM. You pick the model per job, including OpenAI-compatible options, and set global system prompts centrally.

The bigger picture: the line between Make, n8n, and the rest is no longer which one connects more apps. It is which one lets you build agents you can actually trust in production. Make's answer is visibility: see the connections, see the reasoning, see the cost.

If you are on a paid plan, AI Agents are already live. Worth an afternoon of playing.

Question for the group: are you using Make for classic scenario automations, agents, or both? And what is the one workflow you wish you had built sooner?
